accessedFrom.description: Optional start of accessedAt range (inclusive) in ISO 8601 UTC. When both accessedFrom and accessedTo are provided the server SHOULD validate accessedFrom <= accessedTo.

accessedTo.description: Optional end of accessedAt range (inclusive) in ISO 8601 UTC.

sortBy.description: Optional explicit sort key. Supported values: 'accessedAt','-accessedAt','createdAt','-createdAt'. A leading '-' indicates descending order. When provided, server may ignore separate 'order' parameter if the sortBy value contains sign prefix.

order.description: Optional sort direction. Allowed values: 'asc' or 'desc'. When sortBy uses a sign prefix (e.g., '-accessedAt'), the sign takes precedence. This parameter is retained for backward compatibility but servers SHOULD prefer signed sortBy tokens.

id.description: Primary key of the audit-log-access record (UUID).

auditLogId.description: Referenced audit log record id (discussion_board_audit_logs.id). This value is provided to correlate the access record with its parent audit log entry.

accessedAt.description: Timestamp when the audit log entry was accessed (ISO 8601 UTC).

oneOf.description: Classification of the accessor. Allowed exact values: 'moderator', 'administrator', 'system', 'guest'. Use these exact tokens for filtering and RBAC checks.
Classification of the accessor. Allowed exact values: 'moderator', 'administrator', 'system', 'guest'. Use these exact tokens for filtering and RBAC checks.
Classification of the accessor. Allowed exact values: 'moderator', 'administrator', 'system', 'guest'. Use these exact tokens for filtering and RBAC checks.
Classification of the accessor. Allowed exact values: 'moderator', 'administrator', 'system', 'guest'. Use these exact tokens for filtering and RBAC checks.

accessorType.description: Classification of the accessor. Allowed exact values: 'moderator', 'administrator', 'system', 'guest'. Use these exact tokens for filtering and RBAC checks.

accessorId.description: Polymorphic actor identifier when applicable (UUID). Nullable when system or anonymous access. **PII NOTICE**: This field contains PII and must be redacted (returned as null or omitted) for callers without unredacted-audit privileges. Access to unredacted accessorId must itself be audited.

accessorRole.description: Accessor role at time of access (e.g., 'moderator','audit_viewer'). Nullable.

accessPurpose.description: Declared business reason for access (for example: 'appeal_review','legal_request'). Implementation may normalize or canonicalize purpose values.

ip.description: Origin IP address observed for the accessor session, when available. **PII NOTICE**: This is sensitive and may be redacted for non-privileged callers.

userAgent.description: User agent string captured at access time, when available. May be redacted for non-privileged callers.

metadata.description: Optional JSON payload (stored as text) with contextual details about the access (for example: query parameters, filters used). May contain sensitive data and therefore MAY be redacted for callers without unredacted-audit privileges; access to raw metadata must be gated by RBAC and audited.

createdAt.description: Record insertion time for the access event (ISO 8601 UTC).

IDiscussionBoardAuditLogAccess.description: Audit-log-access snapshot mapping to the Prisma model discussion_board_audit_log_accesses. Contains a record of when an audit log entry was accessed and contextual metadata. Sensitive fields (accessorId, ip, userAgent, metadata) must be redacted for callers without unredacted-audit privileges; access to unredacted payloads must itself be recorded in the audit trail.

eventType.description: Filter by audit eventType (for example: 'moderation.action','report.filed'). Exact-match string or null to disable this filter. Nullable; server validates values against known event types.

moderationActionId.description: Filter by moderationActionId (UUID) to find entries related to a specific moderation action. Nullable when not provided.

reportId.description: Filter by originating reportId (UUID). Nullable when not provided.

actorModeratorId.description: Optional filter to restrict results to entries associated with a specific acting moderator (discussion_board_moderator.id). Nullable. Access to results filtered by moderator id and any returned moderator-identifying data MUST be governed by RBAC and audited by the server.

occurredFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound for occurredAt (ISO 8601 date-time). Nullable.

occurredTo.description: Inclusive upper bound for occurredAt (ISO 8601 date-time). Nullable.

textSearch.description: Free-text search applied against eventPayload. PRIVILEGED: queries over eventPayload SHOULD be rate-limited and may require elevated audit privileges. Server implementations MUST enforce redaction rules for non-elevated callers and log accesses to raw payloads.

oneOf.description: Sort by occurredAt ascending.
Sort by occurredAt descending.

sort.description: Sort expression. Allowed values: 'occurredAt', '-occurredAt'. Use '-' prefix for descending order. When null or omitted, server applies default sort (usually '-occurredAt').

IDiscussionBoardModerationAudit.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching moderation audit entries. All filters are optional; UUIDs and datetimes must be validated by the server. NOTE: actor identity filters and free-text queries against eventPayload are privileged operations and should be rate-limited or restricted to elevated roles. Pagination defaults: page=1, limit=20 (max 100).

id.description: Primary identifier of the moderation audit entry (discussion_board_moderation_audit.id).

moderationActionId.description: Optional reference to the related moderation action (discussion_board_moderation_actions.id). Nullable when the audit entry is not linked to a specific action.

reportId.description: Optional reference to the originating report (discussion_board_reports.id). Nullable when the audit entry is not tied to a specific report.

actorModeratorId.description: Optional moderator actor id who triggered or is associated with the audited event (discussion_board_moderator.id). Null for system-generated events. Presence of this field in responses is privileged and may be redacted for non-elevated callers.

actorModerator.description: Optional moderator summary (IDiscussionBoardModerator.ISummary) that provides safe display context for the acting moderator. This convenience field is intended for response payloads only and MUST NOT be accepted in request bodies. Populate only when the caller is authorized to view moderator details.

eventType.description: Canonical event type describing the audited event (for example: 'report.filed','moderation.action','appeal.submitted').

eventPayload.description: Serialized event payload (JSON stored as text) containing the full snapshot of the event. MAY contain sensitive fields (PII). The service MUST enforce privilege checks: for standard moderator roles the implementation SHOULD return a redacted payload or an abbreviated snippet; for elevated administrator/audit roles the full payload may be returned. Access to raw payload MUST be logged in discussion_board_audit_log_accesses and governed by RBAC and retention policies.

occurredAt.description: Timestamp when the audited event occurred (ISO 8601 UTC).

IDiscussionBoardModerationAudit.description: Immutable moderation audit entry recorded in discussion_board_moderation_audit. Fields map directly to the Prisma model and are used for forensic reconstruction and compliance. Implementations MUST apply redaction and privilege gating to `eventPayload` and MUST log any access to raw payloads in discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.

pending_reports_24h.description: Count of reports created in the last 24 hours with status indicating they are pending triage. Non-negative integer (>= 0).

pending_reports_7d.description: Count of reports created in the last 7 days that are still pending. Non-negative integer (>= 0).

actions_breakdown.description: Breakdown of moderation actions aggregated by action_type. Each item is a key/value pair where 'key' is the moderation action_type (for example: 'hide','remove','warn','suspend','ban') and 'value' is the integer count of actions of that type during the measurement window. Values are non-negative integers.

average_processing_times.description: Array of processing-time metrics expressed as IProcessingTime objects. Each item contains 'metric' (string) and 'value_seconds' (number). Values are measured in seconds. Example metrics: 'time_to_first_action' (seconds), 'time_to_resolution' (seconds). Servers SHOULD return averages computed over the requested aggregation window.

recent_high_priority_audits.description: Sanitized short list of recent high-priority moderation audit entries. Each entry is intentionally lightweight and MUST NOT include the full event_payload. Fields provided: id, event_type, occurred_at, short_summary. To access full audit payloads callers require elevated privileges and must use the audit detail endpoint.

generated_at.description: Timestamp when this overview snapshot was generated (ISO 8601 UTC).

IDiscussionBoardModerationOverview.description: Aggregated moderation dashboard overview combining metrics from discussion_board_reports, discussion_board_moderation_actions and sanitized moderation audit entries. This DTO is computed and does not map directly to a single Prisma model. Array properties allow empty arrays (minItems: 0) to indicate no data in the window.

key.description: Aggregation key or label. In moderation breakdown contexts this is typically the moderation action type (e.g., 'hide','remove','warn','suspend','ban').

value.description: Integer value associated with the key (for example, a count). Must be a non-negative integer (>= 0).

IKeyValue.description: Simple aggregation pair used for dashboards and summaries. Represents a label and its numeric count. Use this for action breakdowns, top-N lists, and similar aggregated outputs.

value_seconds.description: Numeric value of the metric measured in seconds (average over the aggregation window).

IProcessingTime.description: Representation of an aggregated processing-time metric measured in seconds.

IDiscussionBoardModerationOverview.IRece.description: Sanitized summary of a moderation audit entry for inclusion in dashboard overview lists. Designed to avoid exposing raw event_payload and sensitive data. Implementations MUST redact reporter PII and other sensitive fields from this short_summary.

id.description: Identifier of the audit entry (discussion_board_moderation_audit.id). Use UUID format.

occurred_at.description: When the event occurred (ISO 8601 UTC). Use date-time format.

short_summary.description: A short, sanitized summary extracted from event_payload suitable for dashboard display. MUST NOT contain reporter PII, raw event_payload JSON, or other sensitive data. Keep concise for UI display.

IDiscussionBoardMember.IRequest.description: Request DTO for moderator/member search and pagination. Filters map to discussion_board_member fields where applicable. This DTO is used only for searching/filtering; it MUST NOT contain secrets such as password_hash. Note: 'email' filter is privileged and must only be honored for callers with elevated privileges; such accesses MUST be audited. Pagination defaults: page=1, limit=20. Server must enforce a maximum limit (recommended max = 100).

email.description: Optional exact-match filter by member email. This filter MUST be accepted only for privileged callers (moderator/admin) and each access SHOULD be recorded in discussion_board_audit_logs for accountability. Public callers must not be able to use this filter.

mfaEnabled.description: Filter by MFA enrollment state. When true, return only members with mfa_enabled = true; when false, return only members with mfa_enabled = false.

includeDeleted.description: When true include soft-deleted accounts (deleted_at IS NOT NULL). Default: false.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based). Default is 1.

limit.description: Maximum items per page. Server MUST enforce a maximum limit (recommended max = 100) to protect the database and ensure predictable pagination. Default is 20.

oneOf.description: Sort by createdAt ascending (client key). Server maps to DB created_at.
Sort by createdAt descending (client key). Server maps to DB created_at.
Sort by username ascending (client key).
Sort by username descending (client key).

sortBy.description: Sort specification using API-friendly keys (camelCase). Allowed values: 'createdAt','-createdAt','username','-username'. The server MUST validate and reject unknown values and map client keys to DB columns server-side.

search.description: Free-text search applied to username and display_name (optional).

IDiscussionBoardMember.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for discussion_board_member. All fields are optional; only editable fields are accepted. Do NOT include id, discussion_board_member_id, created_at, or deleted_at. Server persists a snapshot into discussion_board_article_snapshots prior to applying updates for audit/versioning.

display_name.description: Optional public display name mapping to Prisma column discussion_board_member.display_name. Use this field to update the member's public display name. Note: API surface uses camelCase in some endpoints; this DTO intentionally uses the canonical persisted property name `display_name` to ensure cross-variant consistency with other member DTOs that expose the persisted column name.

password.description: New plain-text password. Must meet password policy: minimum 12 characters and at least three of the following categories: uppercase letter, lowercase letter, number, symbol. The server MUST validate strength, hash the password server-side, and MUST NOT return the password or password_hash in any response. On successful password change the server SHOULD revoke refresh sessions when revokeSessions is true (or per policy) and record an audit entry (without including the raw password).

revokeSessions.description: Optional flag indicating whether the server should revoke all active sessions/refresh tokens for the member after a successful password change. When omitted or false, existing sessions remain subject to server policy. When true the server SHOULD expire discussion_board_member_sessions.expired_at for active sessions or otherwise revoke refresh credentials and record the action in audit logs.

username.description: Optional partial or exact username to search for. Server SHOULD sanitize input before using it in trigram/fuzzy queries to avoid injection and expensive scans.

email.description: Optional exact email filter. This filter is privileged: only elevated callers (moderator/admin) should be allowed to use it. Every use MUST be audited in discussion_board_audit_logs for accountability; the service SHOULD not reveal whether an email exists to unprivileged callers (avoid enumeration).

display_name.description: Optional partial display name to search for (fuzzy matching via trigram index). This property maps to the Prisma column discussion_board_moderator.display_name and aligns naming with moderator summary DTOs that expose the persisted field. Access to display_name-based searches must be logged for audit purposes when used to locate moderator accounts.

createdAtFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound for createdAt (ISO 8601 datetime). Server MUST validate createdAtFrom <= createdAtTo when both are provided.

createdAtTo.description: Inclusive upper bound for createdAt (ISO 8601 datetime). Server MUST validate createdAtFrom <= createdAtTo when both are provided.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based). Default: 1. Server enforces page >= 1.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Default: 20. Server enforces 1 <= limit <= 100 to protect the database and ensure predictable pagination.

oneOf.description: Sort expression. Allowed values: 'createdAt' (ascending) or '-createdAt' (descending). Server validates and rejects other values.
Sort expression. Allowed values: 'createdAt' (ascending) or '-createdAt' (descending). Server validates and rejects other values.

sort.description: Sort expression. Allowed values: 'createdAt' (ascending) or '-createdAt' (descending). Server validates and rejects other values.

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and paginating moderator accounts. This type represents query/filter parameters and is not a direct table representation. Note: the 'email' filter is privileged and must be audited. Pagination defaults: page=1, limit=20; server must enforce limits and validate sort values.

email.description: Optional new email address for the moderator. If provided, the server MUST validate uniqueness across moderator accounts, trigger any verification flows required by policy, and persist updated_at. Example: "moderator.team@discussion.org"

displayName.description: Optional displayName (camelCase) for the moderator. Provide null to clear the display name. This property replaces the snake_case `display_name` to align with public API camelCase conventions and client SDK expectations. Example: "Alice Moderator"

IDiscussionBoardModerator.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for a moderator profile. Accepts only permitted mutable fields. Credential fields (password, password_hash) and the username path key are forbidden and MUST NOT be provided. The server MUST validate email uniqueness and set updated_at upon success.

displayName.description: Optional partial search term to match displayName (case-insensitive, trigram/fuzzy match recommended). Use null to indicate no filter.

ip.description: Exact-match filter for IP address. WARNING: Returning IPs in responses is considered PII. API implementations MUST restrict exposure of IP values to callers with explicit entitlement (moderator/admin) and MUST record access to audit logs (discussion_board_audit_logs). Use null to indicate no ip filter.

createdAtFrom.description: Inclusive lower bound for createdAt (ISO 8601 datetime). When provided the server MUST validate that createdAtFrom <= createdAtTo if createdAtTo is also supplied.

createdAtTo.description: Inclusive upper bound for createdAt (ISO 8601 datetime). When provided the server MUST validate that createdAtFrom <= createdAtTo if createdAtFrom is also supplied.

includeDeleted.description: When true include soft-deleted records (deleted_at != null). Defaults to false.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based). Must be >= 1.

limit.description: Page size for pagination. Must be between 1 and 100. Server SHOULD enforce a conservative upper bound (100).

oneOf.description: Sort by createdAt ascending.
Sort by createdAt descending.
Sort by displayName ascending.
Sort by displayName descending.

sort.description: Sort expression. Allowed values: 'createdAt','-createdAt','displayName','-displayName'. Server MUST validate and reject other values.

IDiscussionBoardGuest.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and paginating discussionBoard guest records. Field names use camelCase to align with the API convention. Validation notes: server MUST enforce page >= 1, limit between 1 and 100, and createdAtFrom <= createdAtTo when both are present. Access to IP values in responses is privileged and must be audited.

IDiscussionBoardSubscription.description: Subscription record linking a member to a polymorphic target. API-facing DTO uses camelCase property names and transforms member FK to a member summary for response safety. Fields mirror the Prisma model while using API naming conventions (camelCase).

member.description: Owning member summary (replaces raw discussion_board_member_id in responses).

oneOf.description: Polymorphic target type 'article'.
Polymorphic target type 'author'.

targetType.description: Polymorphic target type. Allowed exact values: 'article' or 'author'.

targetId.description: UUID of the subscribed target (meaning depends on targetType).

oneOf.description: Deliver notifications immediately.
Accumulate notifications for a daily digest delivery.

deliveryMode.description: Delivery preference for notifications. Allowed exact values: 'immediate' or 'daily_digest'.

lastNotifiedAt.description: Timestamp of the last notification delivered for this subscription; null when none sent.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp (discussion_board_subscriptions.created_at).

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp; when present the record is considered removed for member reads. Nullable.

IDiscussionBoardSubscription.IRequest.description: Search and pagination request for listing a member's subscriptions. Do not include the member identifier in the body when member is supplied via path parameter (memberUsername). Uses camelCase for properties and documents defaults/limits.

limit.description: Number of items per page. Default 20. Maximum 100.

oneOf.description: Filter: immediate delivery mode.
Filter: daily digest delivery mode.

deliveryMode.description: Optional filter for delivery mode. Exact values: 'immediate' or 'daily_digest'.

active.description: Optional filter to return only active (true) or inactive (false) subscriptions.

search.description: Optional free-text search applied to target-related metadata (implementation-specific).

IDiscussionBoardSubscription.ICreate.description: Create DTO for discussion_board_subscriptions. The member identity is provided by the API path (memberUsername) and MUST NOT be supplied in the request body. When target_type == 'author', target_id MUST reference an existing discussion_board_member.id (UUID). When target_type == 'article', target_id MUST reference an existing discussion_board_articles.id (UUID). The server MUST enforce the database uniqueness constraint on (discussion_board_member_id, target_type, target_id) and SHOULD implement idempotent behavior (return existing subscription or 409 Conflict).

oneOf.description: Polymorphic target type: subscription to a specific article. target_id must be the article UUID (discussion_board_articles.id).
Polymorphic target type: subscription to an author. target_id must be the member UUID (discussion_board_member.id).

target_type.description: Polymorphic target type. Allowed values: 'article' or 'author'. The server MUST validate this value and resolve target_id accordingly.

target_id.description: UUID of the target resource. Interpreted according to target_type (e.g., discussion_board_articles.id when target_type='article' or discussion_board_member.id when target_type='author').

oneOf.description: Deliver notifications immediately.
Accumulate notifications for a daily digest delivery.

delivery_mode.description: Delivery preference for the subscription. Allowed values: 'immediate' or 'daily_digest'.

active.description: Whether the subscription is active. Defaults to true when omitted.

IDiscussionBoardNotification.IBulkAction.description: Bulk action descriptor used to request a mutation on a set of notifications. Caller MUST supply the `action` property and either a non-empty `notification_ids` array OR set `apply_to_all` = true. The server MUST validate UUID formats, ownership/authorization over referenced notifications, and audit all bulk actions.

IDiscussionBoardNotification.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and bulk-managing notifications for a member. Use the path-provided memberUsername to scope results; do NOT include recipient identifiers in the body.

status.description: Optional filter by notification status. Allowed values: 'pending','sent','failed'.

subscriptionId.description: Optional filter to limit notifications to a specific subscription id (UUID).

articleId.description: Optional filter to limit notifications related to a specific article (UUID).

hasPayload.description: When true, return only notifications that have a non-empty payload.

scheduledBefore.description: Optional filter to return notifications scheduled before this timestamp (ISO 8601).

scheduledAfter.description: Optional filter to return notifications scheduled after this timestamp (ISO 8601).

q.description: Full-text search query applied to sanitized payload excerpts and related article titles.

oneOf.description: Sort expression. Allowed values: 'scheduledAt','-scheduledAt','createdAt','-createdAt'.
Sort expression. Allowed values: 'scheduledAt','-scheduledAt','createdAt','-createdAt'.
Sort expression. Allowed values: 'scheduledAt','-scheduledAt','createdAt','-createdAt'.
Sort expression. Allowed values: 'scheduledAt','-scheduledAt','createdAt','-createdAt'.

bulkAction.description: Optional bulk action to perform on the matched set. When present, the operation performs the requested mutation and returns the post-action page of results. All bulk actions MUST be audited.

notificationIds.description: Optional explicit target list of notification UUIDs for ad-hoc bulk operations. When present, bulkAction may apply to this list instead of the matched filter set.

IDiscussionBoardNotification.description: Detailed notification object representing a row from discussion_board_notifications. Relation fields are provided as summaries where helpful; raw FK columns are exposed as explicit id properties for implementer clarity. The `payload` may be null when no display payload is present. `deletedAt` is included to reflect soft-delete state in the Prisma model and is nullable.

recipientId.description: Recipient member UUID (maps to discussion_board_notifications.recipient_member_id). Non-nullable in the Prisma schema and therefore present on the DTO. Treat as PII for unprivileged callers; prefer returning `recipient` summary to UI consumers and require audit checks when exposing raw recipientId.

recipient.description: Recipient member summary (derived from discussion_board_notifications.recipient_member_id). Nullable in responses when the server intentionally redacts PII for unprivileged callers; the canonical persisted record includes recipient_member_id.

subscriptionId.description: Optional subscription UUID (maps to discussion_board_notifications.discussion_board_subscription_id). Nullable when the notification was not created from a subscription or when the subscription has been removed.

subscription.description: Optional subscription summary that produced this notification. Replaces raw FK and provides contextual .ISummary object. Nullable when notification not created by a subscription or subscription was removed.

articleId.description: Optional related article UUID (maps to discussion_board_notifications.discussion_board_article_id). Nullable when notification not related to an article or article removed.

article.description: Optional related article summary that triggered the notification. Replaces raw FK. Nullable when notification not related to an article or article removed.

oneOf.description: Opaque payload describing the notification. May contain a small JSON string with display values.

payload.description: Optional opaque payload describing the notification. May be null when no additional display payload is present. Public clients may receive a sanitized excerpt or hasPayload flag instead of full payload.

priority.description: Delivery priority (higher values are processed earlier).

oneOf.description: Timestamp of the last delivery attempt.

lastAttemptedAt.description: Timestamp of the last delivery attempt. Nullable when no attempts have been made.

nextRetryAt.description: Scheduled time for the next retry attempt (backoff). Nullable when no retry is scheduled.

scheduledAt.description: Timestamp when this notification was scheduled to be delivered (discussion_board_notifications.scheduled_at). Non-nullable in Prisma; included here.

sentAt.description: Timestamp when the notification was successfully delivered (nullable).

failReason.description: Optional short failure reason from last attempt (nullable).

createdAt.description: Creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) (discussion_board_notifications.created_at).

deletedAt.description: Soft-delete timestamp if the notification was removed (discussion_board_notifications.deleted_at). Nullable.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationFailure.ISum.description: Summary representation of a single notification delivery failure attempt. Maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_notification_failures. This corrected summary uses the parent FK (notificationId) rather than embedding the parent notification object to prevent circular references and redundancy. Fields are presented in camelCase for API consistency. The parent notification is referenced by id (notificationId) per hierarchical-parent rule.

notificationId.description: Identifier of the parent notification (discussion_board_notifications.id). Child records MUST reference the parent by ID to avoid circular expansion (parent contains failures[]).

attemptNumber.description: Sequential attempt number for this delivery (1-based). Corresponds to discussion_board_notification_failures.attempt_number.

attemptedAt.description: Timestamp when this delivery attempt occurred (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_notification_failures.attempted_at.

errorCode.description: Optional short machine-readable error code returned by the delivery channel (Prisma: discussion_board_notification_failures.error_code).

errorMessage.description: Human-readable error message captured from the delivery attempt (Prisma: discussion_board_notification_failures.error_message). Nullable.

backoffUntil.description: If present, workers should not retry this notification until this timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_notification_failures.backoff_until. Nullable.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_notification_failures.created_at.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationFailure.IReq.description: Request DTO for listing notification failure records. Contains pagination, sorting and filter criteria. Path-identifying fields (memberUsername, notificationId) MUST NOT be supplied in the body. Defaults and limits are explicit to prevent abusive queries.

limit.description: Maximum items per page. Default 20. Server-enforced maximum 100 to mitigate abusive queries.

sort.description: Sort key. Allowed values: 'attemptedAt','-attemptedAt','createdAt','-createdAt'. Use '-' prefix for descending order.

errorMessageQuery.description: Full-text search query applied to errorMessage (uses trigram/GIN index). Use with caution for heavy queries.

id.description: Primary key of the notification failure record (discussion_board_notification_failures.id).

notificationId.description: Foreign key referencing the owning notification (discussion_board_notifications.id). API-facing property name (camelCase) mapped from DB column discussion_board_notification_id. Validate ownership/authorization before returning to callers.

attemptNumber.description: Sequential attempt number for this delivery (1-based). Corresponds to discussion_board_notification_failures.attempt_number.

attemptedAt.description: Timestamp when this delivery attempt occurred (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_notification_failures.attempted_at.

errorCode.description: Optional short machine-readable error code returned by the delivery channel. Nullable; internal codes may be redacted for non-privileged callers.

errorMessage.description: Optional human-readable error message captured from the delivery attempt. Nullable; redact sensitive diagnostics for public callers.

backoffUntil.description: If present, workers SHOULD not retry this notification until this timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_notification_failures.backoff_until. Nullable when no backoff is set.

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_notification_failures.created_at.

IDiscussionBoardNotificationFailure.description: Detailed delivery failure record for a single notification attempt. Maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_notification_failures. Fields mirror persistent columns and are intended for member/support diagnostics. Sensitive internal diagnostics beyond errorCode/errorMessage should be withheld from non-privileged callers.

id.description: Unique identifier of the setting entry (Prisma: discussion_board_settings.id).

value.description: Settings value stored as a string; consumers should parse according to expected type (boolean/number/JSON). Stored as discussion_board_settings.value.

description.description: Optional human-friendly description explaining the purpose of the setting (Prisma: discussion_board_settings.description). Nullable.

isActive.description: Flag indicating whether this setting is active and should be considered by runtime code (maps to discussion_board_settings.is_active).

createdAt.description: Record creation timestamp in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Maps to discussion_board_settings.created_at.

updatedAt.description: Record last modification timestamp in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Maps to discussion_board_settings.updated_at.

IDiscussionBoardSetting.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a runtime configuration setting. Maps to the Prisma model `discussion_board_settings`. This DTO provides the minimal fields required to identify and display a setting in lists or admin UIs. It excludes large structured payloads; the `value` remains a string and consumers interpret its semantic type.

IDiscussionBoardAuditLogAccess.ISummary.description: Summary view of an audit-log access event. Provides minimal information needed when embedding access records in lists or other DTOs. Maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.

id.description: Unique identifier of the audit-log access record (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.id).

accessed_at.description: Timestamp when the audit log was accessed (ISO 8601 UTC) (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.accessed_at). Returned in the same naming/casing as persisted in the DTO to avoid breaking clients; some APIs use camelCase equivalents (accessedAt) elsewhere — consumers should map names as needed.

accessor_type.description: Actor classification that performed the access (e.g., 'moderator','administrator','system'). Maps to discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.accessor_type.

accessor_id.description: Polymorphic actor identifier (UUID) when applicable (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.accessor_id). Nullable when accessor is not persisted or has been anonymized. THIS FIELD CONTAINS PII and implementations MUST redact it (return null) for callers without unredacted-audit privileges.

accessor.description: Reference to the accessor summary. Polymorphic: may be a member or a moderator summary depending on accessor_type. Nullable to reflect nullable accessor_id. Use this convenience object for display; sensitive fields in the embedded summaries are already sanitized.

accessor_role.description: Accessor role at time of access (optional) — useful for retrospective RBAC checks (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.accessor_role).

access_purpose.description: Declared business reason for the access (e.g., 'appeal_review', 'legal_request') (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.access_purpose).

ip.description: IP address of the accessor session when available (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.ip). Considered sensitive PII and MUST be redacted for callers without audit entitlement. When redacted the API MUST return explicit null rather than omitting the property.

user_agent.description: User agent string of the accessor session when available (discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.user_agent). Nullable and may be redacted for callers without privilege. When redacted the API MUST return explicit null.

audit_log.description: Parent audit log summary referenced by this access record. Replaces raw foreign key discussion_board_audit_log_id for client responses. Required because underlying FK is non-nullable in Prisma.

created_at.description: Record insertion timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Maps to discussion_board_audit_log_accesses.created_at and is required for traceability.

IDiscussionBoardModerationAudit.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a moderation audit entry (append-only). Maps to the Prisma model discussion_board_moderation_audit.

id.description: Unique identifier of the moderation audit entry (discussion_board_moderation_audit.id).

event_type.description: Canonical event type (e.g., 'report.filed','moderation.action','appeal.submitted') (discussion_board_moderation_audit.event_type). Use the exact canonical event type strings defined by the system.

occurred_at.description: Timestamp when the audited event occurred (ISO 8601 UTC) (discussion_board_moderation_audit.occurred_at). Returned using the persisted naming to remain consistent with DB columns in other summary DTOs.

actor_moderator_id.description: Optional moderator actor id when applicable (discussion_board_moderation_audit.actor_moderator_id). Nullable for system-generated events. THIS FIELD IS PII: return null for non-privileged callers.

actor_moderator.description: Summary of the moderator who acted (if applicable). Use moderator summary to provide contextual information without exposing sensitive moderator internals. Nullable when actor_moderator_id is null. Population of this convenience field is privilege-checked by the server.

moderation_action.description: Optional reference to the moderation action related to this audit record (derived from discussion_board_moderation_audit.moderation_action_id). Nullable when not applicable or when the action has been removed. Provided as a summary object for safe embedding.

report.description: Optional reference to the report related to this audit record (derived from discussion_board_moderation_audit.report_id). Nullable when not applicable. Returned as a sanitized summary for triage UIs.

event_payload_snippet.description: Short human-readable snippet of the event payload suitable for list displays. kind.description: Discriminator value indicating this variant references a new attachment via storage_key.

scenario.draft: Test successful guest join flow: Call POST /auth/guest/join with a minimal valid payload (e.g., { displayName: 'guest-automated-test' }). Verify response status is 201 (or configured success code) and that the response body contains an authorized payload referencing the persisted guest: guest id, display_name, created_at and updated_at timestamps in ISO 8601 format, and an access + refresh token pair. Assert tokens contain guest id in claims or that the returned authorized object references the same guest id. Confirm tokens are short-lived by verifying expiry metadata if present. This scenario focuses on end-to-end creation and token issuance for a new guest context. Dependencies: [] (join creates its own user context).

Test successful guest token refresh: 1) Create a fresh guest context by calling POST /auth/guest/join and capture the issued refresh token and guest id. 2) Call POST /auth/guest/refresh with the valid refresh token. 3) Verify the response returns a renewed access token (and optionally a rotated refresh token) and an authorized payload referencing the same guest id. 4) Confirm the guest row exists (deleted_at is null) and new token lifetimes are short-lived. Dependencies: authentication first (POST /auth/guest/join to obtain initial tokens).

scenario.draft: Validate the public category listing workflow and filtering behavior. Steps: 1) Create a moderator account via POST /auth/moderator/join to obtain moderator credentials (new user context). 2) Using the moderator's token, create multiple categories via POST /discussionBoard/moderator/categories (at least two categories: one active and one inactive) to seed data for listing. 3) As an unauthenticated client, call PATCH /discussionBoard/categories with default pagination to retrieve the category list and verify HTTP 200. Validate that the response contains pagination metadata (total, page, limit) and that returned items map to created categories (id, name, slug, is_active, created_at). 4) Exercise filtering: call PATCH /discussionBoard/categories with isActive=true and confirm only active categories are returned. 5) Exercise search: call PATCH /discussionBoard/categories with a partial search string that matches name or slug and confirm relevant categories are in results. 6) Verify soft-delete semantics: soft-delete a category (via moderator endpoint) or create a category then soft-delete it and confirm it is excluded from public listings by default. 7) Validate error handling: calling PATCH with invalid pagination (limit > 100 or page < 1) returns 400 with validation details. Expected outcomes: listing succeeds (200) with correct pagination and filtering behavior; invalid inputs return 400; soft-deleted categories are excluded by default.

scenario.draft:
Validate that an authenticated member can list their active sessions and that returned session items contain the expected session metadata. Steps:
1) Create a brand-new member context by calling POST /auth/member/join with unique test registration data. Capture the issued access token from the join response.
2) Call GET /auth/member/sessions with the member access token in Authorization header.
3) Verify HTTP 200 and that the response is a paginated sessions page. Assert that each returned session item includes the fields: id (UUID), ip (string or null), href (string or null), referrer (string or null), created_at (ISO 8601 datetime) and expired_at (ISO 8601 datetime or null).
4) If the system issues a session on join, assert there is at least one session whose id correlates to the authenticated member; otherwise accept an empty list but validate shape and pagination metadata.
5) Confirm that session items do not expose refresh/access token values or password hashes.
Business validations: listing is owner-scoped (only sessions for the authenticated member are returned), response excludes sensitive token values, and pagination metadata is present and consistent.
Failure cases to consider: unauthorized (no token) returns 401; malformed token returns 401; unexpected payload shapes return 5xx.

scenario.draft:
Validate that a member can revoke (erase) one of their own sessions and that the session is removed from subsequent listings. Steps:
1) Create a brand-new member context by calling POST /auth/member/join and capture the access token (new user context must use join only).
2) Call GET /auth/member/sessions with the access token to retrieve the current active sessions for the member and capture a valid sessionId from the returned list. If no session exists after join, record the scenario precondition and ensure the test harness can still assert idempotent revoke semantics by creating or selecting a session if supported by the system.
3) Call DELETE /auth/member/sessions/{sessionId} with the member access token and the captured sessionId in the path.
4) Expect HTTP 204 No Content (or acceptable alternative per product policy). Then call GET /auth/member/sessions again and assert the revoked sessionId is no longer present in the returned list.
5) Validate business rules: only the owning member (or authorized admin) can revoke the session; attempting to revoke the same session a second time returns 404 or idempotent success per policy; unauthorized callers receive 403/401.
Failure and edge cases: revoking non-existent session returns 404; attempting to revoke a session owned by another member returns 403; validate auditability where relevant (audit record created) if test harness supports it.

Validate the response is 201 Created and capture the returned slug (or use the known slug value).
3) Call GET /discussionBoard/tags/{tagSlug} (replace {tagSlug} with the created tag slug) as an unauthenticated public request.

5) Additional assertions: ensure the response does not contain sensitive fields and that the returned slug is normalized (lower-case) if applicable. Confirm the record is excluded from archived results only when includeArchived is not requested.
Expected outcomes: 200 OK, response payload matches created tag summary, public visibility enforced (no authentication required).

scenario.draft:
Test moderator token refresh (success and failure paths).

Success path:
1) Create a new moderator account using POST /auth/moderator/join with a valid username, email and password (new user context - join only). Capture the returned authorized response and extract refreshToken and accessToken and moderator id.
2) Simulate access token expiration (or simply call the refresh endpoint) and call POST /auth/moderator/refresh with the captured refreshToken.
3) Verify the response is 200 and returns a renewed IAuthorized payload with a new access token (and possibly a rotated refresh token). Validate returned moderator id matches the original id and that token claims correspond to the moderator actor. Confirm renewed access token can be used against a moderator-protected endpoint (implicit verification step).

Failure and edge cases:
A) Use an expired/invalid refresh token and expect 401 Unauthorized or a well-formed error indicating invalid/expired token.
B) Soft-deleted moderator: after creating a moderator (join), mark the moderator record as deleted (simulate by test harness or DB) then attempt refresh with the previously issued refresh token and expect the endpoint to reject renewal (403/404 per product policy). Verify no new tokens are issued.
C) Replay/rotation check: if refresh rotation is enabled, verify that using a rotated refresh token (old one) is rejected after rotation (409/401 as per product policy).

Validation points:
- Successful response contains IDiscussionBoardModerator.IAuthorized structure and new tokens.
- Moderator id consistency between join and refresh.
- Proper error codes for invalid/expired/revoked tokens.
- No escalation of privileges during refresh.

Notes:
This scenario uses a new user context created by /auth/moderator/join to obtain initial credentials; login is not used in this scenario per the test-user-context rules (join-only for new contexts).

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as moderator to obtain initial access/refresh tokens for refresh flow testing.

scenario.draft:
Test moderator change-password workflow and session revocation behavior.

Positive (happy) path:
1) Create a new moderator via POST /auth/moderator/join with a known password (new user context - join only). Capture the returned access and refresh tokens and moderator id.
2) Call POST /auth/moderator/password/change authenticated as the created moderator (use the join-issued access token) with payload { currentPassword: <original>, newPassword: <strong-new-password> } where newPassword meets strength policy.
3) Expect 200 OK and verify response contains moderator summary (no password_hash). Confirm the service revoked existing sessions by attempting to use the previously captured refresh token: POST /auth/moderator/refresh with the old refresh token should fail (401/403) or otherwise indicate revocation.
4) (Optional verification) Attempt to use the old access token and expect it to be rejected by protected moderator endpoints, confirming session revocation.

Negative and edge cases:
A) Wrong current password: call change-password with an incorrect currentPassword and expect 403 Forbidden or 400 with an explanatory message — the password must not be changed.
B) Weak new password: call change-password with a newPassword that fails strength validation (e.g., too short) and expect 400 with validation details.
C) Soft-deleted moderator: if the moderator record is soft-deleted between join and change attempt, expect the endpoint to reject the request (403/404) and not change password.

Validation points:
- Password change must update discussion_board_moderator.password_hash server-side (not returned) and updated_at must be updated.
- Active sessions (discussion_board_moderator_sessions) must be invalidated; refresh with old refresh token must fail.
- Proper error codes and messages for incorrect current password and weak new passwords.

Notes:
This scenario uses join to create the moderator (new user context). Do NOT use login in the same scenario. All authentication for the protected call is established using the tokens returned by join.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as moderator to obtain initial credentials used to authenticate the password-change request and to validate session revocation.

scenario.draft:
Successful retrieval of a notification delivery failure by the notification owner.

Steps:
1) Register a new member (new user context) via POST /auth/member/join with realistic member data (username, email, password) to obtain an access token and member context. Extract memberUsername and access token from the response.
2) Using the member token, create an article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles to produce content that could generate notifications. Persist the returned articleId.
3) (Test setup) Ensure there is a notification addressed to the created member and a delivery failure record for attemptNumber (this may be created by test fixture or a background job in the test environment). The failure record must include attempt_number, attempted_at, error_code (e.g., "SMTP_TIMEOUT"), and an error_message describing the failure.
4) Perform GET /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/notifications/{notificationId}/failures/{attemptNumber} authenticated as the member (Authorization: Bearer <token>).
5) Validate response:
   - HTTP 200
   - Response body contains id, discussion_board_notification_id equals notificationId, attempt_number equals attemptNumber
   - attempted_at is an ISO-8601 datetime
   - error_code is a known error token (e.g., "SMTP_TIMEOUT" or "BOUNCED") and error_message is a non-empty string
   - backoff_until is either null or a valid ISO-8601 datetime if present

Business validations:
- The operation must return full diagnostic fields for the owner (no elevated privileges required beyond member ownership).
- The request must fail if the notification does not belong to the authenticated member.

Expected outcome: member successfully retrieves detailed delivery failure information for their notification attempt.

scenario.draft:
Test soft-delete (remove) of a moderator account by username. Workflow:

1) Create a new moderator account using POST /auth/moderator/join with unique username/email and store the returned authorization tokens and the created moderator username. This establishes a fresh moderator actor context (new user context via join).
2) Using the access token returned by the join response, call DELETE /discussionBoard/moderator/moderators/{moderatorUsername} where {moderatorUsername} is the username created in step (1). Validate that the call succeeds with HTTP 204 No Content.
3) Post-conditions: confirm the server recorded the soft-delete by setting deleted_at on the moderator row and that active sessions for that moderator are revoked (previously-issued tokens are invalid for protected moderator endpoints).

Validation points:
- The DELETE request must be authorized using the access token obtained from the moderator join in step (1).

scenario.draft:

4) As the authenticated moderator, call POST /discussionBoard/moderator/members/{memberUsername}/subscriptions with payload { target_type: 'article', target_id: <articleId>, delivery_mode: 'immediate', active: true }.
5) Validate success: HTTP 201 Created and response contains a subscription record referencing the member and target article (discussion_board_subscriptions row persisted).
6) Negative checks: repeating the same create call should return 409 Conflict due to the junction uniqueness constraint (discussion_board_member_id, target_type, target_id). Attempting the same POST as a non-moderator (e.g., another member) should return 403 Forbidden.

Validation points:
- Ensure article exists before attempting subscription (created in step 2).
- Ensure moderator credentials are used for the moderator-scoped creation step.

scenario.draft:
Test the unsubscribe (soft-delete) workflow for a member subscription. Steps:
1) Create a new member context using POST /auth/member/join to obtain member credentials (new user context per rules). Validate join succeeded and extract access token and returned member username.
2) Using the member's token, create a new article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles to obtain an articleId. Validate 201 Created and capture articleId.
3) Using the same member token, create a subscription for the member to that article via POST /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/subscriptions. Validate 201 Created and capture subscription existence for (member, targetType='article', targetId=articleId).
4) Perform the target operation: DELETE /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/subscriptions/{targetType}/{targetId} using the member token to unsubscribe from the article. Validate the call returns 204 No Content (idempotent behavior). Confirm the subscription row is soft-deleted (deleted_at set) by attempting to GET the subscription (expect 404) or by re-creating the subscription (expect 201 or 409 depending on idempotency policy).
Validation points and business rules to assert:
- Authentication is required: requests without token must be rejected (401).
- Ownership/authorization: member may only unsubscribe their own subscriptions; attempts by other members must return 403.
- Idempotency: deleting an already-deleted subscription should succeed (204) and not error.
- Referential integrity: unsubscribing a non-existent subscription (targetId not existing or not associated with member) should return 404.
- After successful unsubscribe the subscription should be excluded from active delivery flows (active=false) and preserved for audit (deleted_at populated).

Test searching and bulk-managing notifications for a member. Steps:

3) Create a subscription for the member to the article via POST /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/subscriptions so notification-generation conditions are met.
4) Allow the system to generate notification entries (background job). Implement test polling until notifications appear.
5) Call PATCH /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername}/notifications with the member token to search/filter notifications (page, limit, filter by unread) and validate returned summaries. Verify the summary does not expose raw payload PII and includes hasPayload/excerpt flags.
6) Use the same PATCH endpoint to perform a bulk operation (for example mark matched notifications as read) and verify the bulk update is applied atomically and audit entries are recorded.
Validation points and business rules to assert:
- Authentication: endpoint requires member auth; unauthenticated requests must be rejected (401).
- Ownership: member can only list and manage their own notifications; other-member attempts must be rejected (403).
- Pagination and filtering: validate page/limit defaults, max limit enforcement, and correct filtering by criteria (unread, by articleId, by subscriptionId).
- Bulk operations: verify atomicity (either all matched notifications updated or none) and that summaries returned do not leak sensitive payloads (payload only returned to authorized callers or as sanitized excerpt).
- Side effects: after bulk mark-as-read, subsequent searches reflect updated notification state and delivery flows are adjusted accordingly.

Validation points: ensure processed_at and closed_at are valid ISO-8601 datetimes and chronology is enforced (processed_at >= created_at; closed_at >= processed_at). End-to-end scenario validating the global search endpoint across multiple resource types (articles, comments, attachments, tags) and filtering by category and tag. Steps:
1. Create a moderator account (POST /auth/moderator/join) to perform taxonomy setup (categories, tags).
2. As moderator, create a category (POST /discussionBoard/moderator/categories) that will be assigned to the test article.
3. As moderator, create one or more tags (POST /discussionBoard/moderator/tags) referenced by the article.
4. Create a member account (POST /auth/member/join) to author content.
5. As the member, create an article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles) with the created category and tags; set title and content containing unique test keywords for search.
6. As the same member, add a comment to the article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/comments) containing another unique keyword to verify comment search.
7. As the same member, upload an attachment for the article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/attachments) with an original filename that contains a search keyword to verify attachment search.
8. Call PATCH /discussionBoard/search/global with queries and filters: a) full-text query matching article title/content, b) filter by category id, c) filter by tag slug, and d) request pagination and highlight. Validate:
   - Response status is 200 and pagination metadata is present.
   - At least one article result matches the article title/content and includes article summary fields (id, title, excerpt, published_at).
   - At least one comment result includes comment excerpt and parent article reference.
   - At least one attachment result contains original_filename and is_image flag (or metadata) and links back to article id.
   - Tag results include tag name/slug when searching by tag.
   - Filtering by category and tag reduces results appropriately and combined filters return the intersection of expected items.
9. Edge-cases: Verify that searching for a nonexistent random token returns an empty result set with 200 and correct pagination metadata.

Expected outcomes: Search returns unified, typed results with correct discriminator type values ("article","comment","attachment","tag"), correct pagination, and respects soft-delete and moderation visibility rules (only published/visible resources are returned).

6. Call GET /discussionBoard/statistics/article-activity with start_date and end_date covering the created data and validate:
   - Response status is 200 and the returned time-series contains buckets for each day in the range.

7. Edge-cases: Request a date range with no data and verify the endpoint returns an empty series or zeroed counts with 200.

Expected outcomes: The endpoint returns accurate aggregated metrics consistent with created test data, excludes soft-deleted or hidden resources, and provides correctly-formatted time-bucketed series suitable for dashboards.

scenario.draft:
Validate moderation queue aggregation and prioritized triage flow for moderator actors. Steps:
1) Create fresh authentication contexts: register a new moderator (POST /auth/moderator/join) and a new member (POST /auth/member/join) to act as the reporter/creator. Obtain moderator and member auth tokens.
2) Using the member context, create test data: (a) create an article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles), (b) create a comment under that article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/comments), and (c) create an attachment for the article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/attachments). Ensure each creation returns resource ids.
3) Still using the member context, file multiple reports (POST /discussionBoard/member/reports) that target the created article, the comment, and the attachment. Create at least three reports (some duplicates across targets) so the system has aggregated reportCounts to surface priority targets.
4) Using the moderator context, call PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/moderationQueue with filters to surface high-priority targets and includeReporterContext=true (simulate a moderator with audit privilege). Verify the response:
   - status 200 and paginated results
   - each returned item includes a reportCount aggregation per (target_type,target_id)
   - targets with more reports appear higher when sorted by priority
   - reporter context (reporter_member_id and reporter display_name) is present only because includeReporterContext was requested and the moderator context has audit privileges; session-level PII (IPs/emails) must be omitted unless explicitly allowed
   - verify at least one returned summary references the article/comment/attachment created earlier

scenario.draft:
Validate batch update rejects unknown keys and preserves transactional semantics. Steps:
1) Create a new moderator context using POST /auth/moderator/join and obtain an access token.
2) Ensure at least one valid setting key exists via POST /discussionBoard/moderator/settings (e.g., key="feature_x_enabled").
3) Call PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/settings with a batch payload that includes one valid key update and one non-existent key (e.g., { key: "non_existent_key", value: "x" }). Include Authorization header with moderator token.
4) Assert the server rejects the batch with a clear 400/404-level error describing which keys were invalid and that no partial updates were applied (transactional behavior). Verify the valid key remains unchanged after the failed request.
Validation points: error message enumerates invalid keys, atomicity prevents partial application, proper status code used (400/404) and audit logs reflect attempted update with failure record.
Expected outcome: 400/404 with detailed error, no settings mutated.

scenario.draft:
End-to-end scenario validating moderator-driven soft-delete of an article attachment and its auditable side-effects.

Steps:
1) Create a NEW member context (POST /auth/member/join) to produce a member access token. This member will create the article and upload the attachment. Save the returned access token and member id.
2) Create a NEW moderator context (POST /auth/moderator/join) to obtain moderator credentials. Use the moderator token later to perform the soft-delete.
3) Using the member token, create an article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles) and capture the generated articleId. Verify response 201 and articleId present.
4) Using the same member token, upload or persist attachment metadata to the article (POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/attachments). Capture the returned attachmentId and assert the persisted attachment record (id, storage_key, original_filename) is returned.
5) As the moderator (Bearer moderatorToken), call DELETE /discussionBoard/moderator/articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId}.
   - Expected: HTTP 204 No Content; the test asserts soft-delete semantics by subsequently attempting to retrieve the attachment metadata (GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId}) and verifying it is treated as deleted (deleted_at populated) or is not visible to public listing. If GET for moderators is available, assert deleted_at is set.
   - Verify authorization: a non-moderator (member token) attempting the same delete should only be allowed if the member is the uploader/article author; otherwise receive 403. The primary assertion is that the moderator can perform the soft-delete.
6) Assert auditability: where available, verify a moderation action or audit log entry was created; if audit endpoints are not available, assert the attachment is no longer visible in public listings.

Validation points / expected outcomes:
- Creating article and attachment succeed with 201 and valid ids.
- Moderator join returns an authorized payload with tokens.
- DELETE as moderator returns 204 and subsequent reads treat the attachment as soft-deleted (not visible to public listing; deleted_at set when accessible).
- Operation enforces ownership/role checks: member who is not uploader/author should not be able to delete (403) while moderator can.

This scenario focuses on business rules: role-based authorization (moderator elevated privilege), soft-delete semantics (deleted_at set), and auditability of moderator actions — not on low-level input validation errors.

E2E scenario validating public retrieval of comments for an article after member-created content is persisted.

Steps:

3) Using the member token, create a visible comment on that article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/comments. Capture the commentId and confirm the response includes the persisted comment (id, content, author summary).
4) As an anonymous/public caller (no auth header), call PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments with pagination (page=1, limit=20) and optional search filters to retrieve the comment list for the article.
   - Expected: HTTP 200 with paginated envelope containing the created comment in the results. The returned comment summary must include id, content excerpt and author summary (id, username, display_name) — and must NOT include sensitive fields (email, password_hash).
5) Additional validation: create an extra comment and ensure listing returns both entries and that deleted/hidden comments (if simulated) are excluded from public results.

Validation points / expected outcomes:
- Member join and article/comment creation succeed (201) and return IDs.
- Public PATCH /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/comments returns 200 and includes the created comment(s) in the paginated data array.
- The response excludes soft-deleted or is_hidden=true comments from public listings.
- The scenario focuses on business behavior: correct public visibility rules, correct association of comments to the article, and presence of author summary fields in responses rather than sensitive data.

scenario.draft:
Test authenticated member self-update (display_name and password change) using the member update endpoint. Workflow:
1) Create a fresh member using POST /auth/member/join to obtain credentials and the created member's username and initial tokens.
2) Using the created member's authorization (access token returned by join), call PUT /discussionBoard/member/members/{memberUsername} with a payload that updates display_name and provides a new plaintext password that meets strength rules (>=12 chars, mix of character classes).
3) Validate the response:
   - Status 200 and returned member object reflects the updated display_name and has updated_at more recent than created_at.
   - The response MUST NOT include password_hash or any sensitive credential data.
4) Verify side-effects:
   - Option A (if product enforces session revocation on password change): attempt to use the original access/refresh token for a protected endpoint and assert tokens are invalidated.
   - Option B (if revocation not enforced): assert new login with updated password succeeds.
5) Negative cases to include in tests at runtime:
   - Attempt update without Authorization header and assert 401/403 as appropriate.
   - Attempt update as a different member: create an additional member via POST /auth/member/join and attempt the update with that member's token; assert 403 Forbidden.
Validation points:
- Update succeeds only when authenticated as the target member.
- Password strength is enforced server-side; weak passwords yield 400 with descriptive message.
- password_hash is never returned in responses.
- updated_at is updated after successful change.
Notes:
- Follow the 'New User Context' rule: create the member via join to obtain a fresh test subject. Use the same join operation at runtime to create any additional member needed for negative-case checks; do not list duplicate identical endpoint entries in the dependencies array.

6) Validate the response: status 200 and a paginated envelope containing the expected failure summaries. Verify filter semantics (e.g., filtering by error_code returns only matching items), pagination metadata is correct, and that non-owner access is rejected with 401/403.

scenario.draft:
This scenario validates the complete member password-reset request workflow and verifies non-enumeration behavior and proper persistence of a reset record.

Steps:
1) Create a fresh member account via POST /auth/member/join with a unique username and email. Record the created member id for verification.
2) Consume the email verification token produced by the join operation by calling POST /auth/member/email/verify (use the test harness or DB lookup to obtain the single-use verification token). Assert the verification call succeeds and the member is marked verified (email verification record consumed).
3) Call the target endpoint POST /auth/member/password/request with the member's email (or username if supported) to request a password reset. Assert the HTTP response indicates the request was accepted (200/202/204 depending on implementation) and does not reveal whether the account exists (response body and status should be indistinguishable for existing and non-existing accounts).
4) Verify a discussion_board_password_resets row was created for the member: query the test database or test harness for a reset record referencing the created member id and assert created_at is present, expires_at is in the future, and consumed_at is null.
5) Perform a second request with the same email immediately to exercise resend/rate-limit logic. Expect either a successful idempotent response or a rate-limited response (429) depending on product policy; assert the service enforces rate limits or dedup behavior without exposing account existence.
6) Call POST /auth/member/password/request with a clearly non-existent email and assert the HTTP response matches the response from step 3 (non-enumeration): no difference in status/body that would allow email enumeration. Additionally verify that no reset record was created for that non-existent identity.

Validation points (business rules):
- The API must not reveal whether an email exists. Tests assert the same response semantics for existing and non-existing addresses.
- A reset record is persisted for the real member with expires_at set and consumed_at null.
- Repeated requests are handled according to policy (idempotent or rate-limited) without exposing account presence.

Expected outcomes:
- Member creation and email verification succeed.
- Password reset request returns an accepted response and does not leak account existence.
- A single reset token row exists for the created member with valid timestamps.
- Repeated requests are handled according to policy without exposing account presence.

scenario.draft:
This scenario verifies the end-to-end password reset flow that consumes a single-use reset token, updates the member's password, and enforces single-use and expiry semantics.

Steps:
1) Create a fresh member via POST /auth/member/join. Ensure the account is persisted and record the member id and initial authentication credentials.
2) Trigger a reset token by calling POST /auth/member/password/request for that member's email. Confirm the request returns an accepted response and a reset record is created in the persistence layer.
3) Obtain the single-use reset token produced in step 2 via the test harness (e.g., read the persisted discussion_board_password_resets.token from the DB or intercept the outbound email in test environment). Validate that the token exists, that its expires_at is in the future, and consumed_at is null.
4) Call the target endpoint POST /auth/member/password/reset with the valid token and a new strong password that meets policy. Assert the endpoint returns success (200/201) and the response either returns a member summary or an authorization payload per implementation.
5) Verify side-effects:
   - The discussion_board_password_resets row has consumed_at populated (token consumed exactly once).
   - The member's password_hash has changed; verify by attempting authentication: POST /auth/member/login with the new password succeeds and login with the old password fails.
   - Optionally verify active sessions were revoked or session expiry updated according to policy (if session listing/revocation endpoints are available in test harness).
6) Attempt to reuse the same reset token: call POST /auth/member/password/reset again with the same token and a different password. Assert the operation fails with the expected error (invalid/expired token, e.g., 401/400) and that consumed_at was not overwritten.
7) Test token expiry edge case: simulate token expiry (set token.expires_at in the past via test harness) and assert that POST /auth/member/password/reset rejects the expired token (401/400) and no password change occurs.

Validation points (business rules):
- Reset token is single-use: consumed_at is set on successful consume and subsequent attempts are rejected.
- Expired tokens are rejected and do not change password_hash.
- After successful reset, the member can authenticate with the new password and cannot authenticate with the old one.

Expected outcomes:
- Reset successfully changes the member password when using a valid, unexpired token.
- Token is consumed exactly once and cannot be reused.
- Expired or invalid tokens are rejected without altering member credentials.

scenario.draft:
Public retrieval workflow for a single article attachment's metadata, including verification of visibility rules and metadata correctness.

Steps:
1) Create a new member (new user context) via POST /auth/member/join to act as the article author.
2) Verify the member's email using POST /auth/member/email/verify (consume the join-generated token) so the member can publish content (ensures article can be published if required by business logic).
3) Create an article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles (optionally request state='published' if the create DTO supports it after verification). Capture articleId.
4) Upload an attachment via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/attachments to persist discussion_board_attachments metadata and capture attachmentId.
5) As an anonymous/public caller (no auth), call GET /discussionBoard/articles/{articleId}/attachments/{attachmentId} to retrieve attachment metadata.

Validations and expected outcomes (success):
- GET returns 200 OK with the attachment DTO containing original_filename, mime_type, size, is_image and a downloadUrl/publicUrl (or storage metadata) appropriate for public consumption.
- The attachment is correctly scoped to the provided articleId; if the attachment is requested with mismatched articleId the endpoint returns 404.
- If the parent article is in a public-visible state (published) and not soft-deleted, the attachment metadata is accessible to public callers.

Failure and edge-case validations:
A) Non-existent attachmentId or mismatched articleId: expect 404 Not Found.
B) Parent article hidden/pending_review/deleted: expect 404 or 403 per policy (verify the API returns non-disclosure 404 to public callers when content is not public).
C) Attachment metadata should not leak internal-only fields such as raw storage_key to public callers; expect a signed downloadUrl or CDN URL instead.

Additional checks:
- Confirm that created_at timestamps on the returned DTO are correctly populated and ISO 8601 formatted.
- Verify that attempting to access the metadata for an attachment whose record exists but whose storage_key has been quarantined results in 403/422 or metadata indicating quarantine state (per product behavior).

Rationale: This scenario validates that attachment metadata retrieval is usable by public consumers for published content, while enforcing visibility and privacy rules and ensuring returned metadata is safe for public use.

scenario.draft:
Purpose: Verify that a moderator can retrieve a single audit-log-access record and that access controls, redaction, and audit-access recording behave correctly.

Step-by-step workflow (implementable, deterministic):
1. Create a new member account (POST /auth/member/join) to act as the content author and reporter. Capture member credentials/token.
2. Create a new moderator account (POST /auth/moderator/join) to act as the moderator. Capture moderator credentials/token.
3. Using the member token, create an article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles and capture articleId.
4. Using the member token, create a comment on the article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/comments and capture commentId (optional for comment-target reports).
5. Using the member token, file a report via POST /discussionBoard/member/reports that targets the created article or comment; capture reportId.
6. Using the moderator token, create a moderation action via POST /discussionBoard/moderator/moderation/actions referencing the reportId so that moderation audit entries are generated.
7. Ensure an audit-log-access record exists for retrieval (either produced by system hooks when audit reads occur or by causing a recorded access); obtain auditLogAccessId.
8. Using the moderator token, call GET /discussionBoard/moderator/auditLogAccesses/{auditLogAccessId} and validate:
   - 200 OK and well-formed audit-access DTO when called by moderator
   - Sensitive fields (metadata, accessor_id/ip) are redacted unless elevated audit privileges are present
   - 401/403 for non-moderator or unauthenticated calls
   - 400 for invalid UUID format, 404 for missing id

Validation points: returned object contains id (UUID), discussion_board_audit_log_id (UUID), accessor_type, accessor_id (may be redacted), accessor_role, access_purpose, ip (may be redacted), user_agent, metadata (redacted or present depending on privilege).

scenario.draft:
Purpose: Validate moderator search, filtering, pagination, and redaction behavior when querying moderation audit entries (discussion_board_moderation_audit).

Step-by-step workflow (implementable, deterministic):
1. Create a member account via POST /auth/member/join to act as content author and reporter. Capture member token.
2. Create a moderator account via POST /auth/moderator/join to perform moderation actions. Capture moderator token.
3. As the member, create an article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles and capture articleId.
4. As the member, create one or more comments under the article via POST /discussionBoard/member/articles/{articleId}/comments to create additional reportable targets.
5. As the member, file reports via POST /discussionBoard/member/reports that reference the article and/or comments to populate discussion_board_reports.
6. As the moderator, create moderation actions via POST /discussionBoard/moderator/moderation/actions referencing the created reports; these will generate moderation audit entries.
7. As the moderator, call PATCH /discussionBoard/moderator/moderationAudits with filters (moderator id, action_type, occurred_at range), page=1, small limit to validate pagination and ordering.

Validation points: response is HTTP 200 with paginated ISummary envelope, each summary includes id, moderation_action_id, report_id, actor_moderator_id, event_type, occurred_at and event_payload is redacted for standard moderator role. Verify pagination metadata (total, page, limit) and that filtering returns only matching records. Invalid inputs produce 400; unauthorized callers produce 401/403.
